title: Hatim of the Tribe of Tayy
summary: Among the nomadic tribes of ancient Arabia, none was more celebrated than Hatim of the noble tribe of Tayy. His open hand was like the rain of spring; he never turned away a beg...
keywords: hatim of the tribe of tayy
full_text:
Among the nomadic tribes of ancient Arabia, none was more celebrated than Hatim of the noble tribe of Tayy. His open hand was like the rain of spring; he never turned away a beggar, never refused a traveler shelter, and slaughtered his prize horses whenever a stranger arrived at his campfire.

The King of Rome, hearing of Hatim’s fame, felt an itch of royal jealousy. He thought: 'Can a mere desert nomad surpass an emperor in magnificence?' The king dispatched an envoy with secret orders to test Hatim’s generosity to the uttermost: the envoy was to demand Hatim’s favorite stallion, a black Arabian steed famed for unmatched speed and beauty, which Hatim loved above all his possessions.

The royal envoy arrived at Hatim’s camp during a torrential winter storm. The desert was flooded, game was impossible to find, and the livestock were grazing three days' journey away. Hatim welcomed the shivering stranger into his tent, dried his garments before the fire, and served him a sumptuous roast of savory meat.

After the banquet, the envoy stood and delivered the Roman emperor’s request: 'O Hatim, my master demands your famous black stallion as a token of your renowned generosity.'

Hatim’s eyes filled with tears, and he struck his hands together in sorrow. 'Alas, noble guest!' cried Hatim. 'Why did you not speak your request when you first stepped across my threshold? When you arrived drenched and starving in the midnight storm, I had no meat to set before you, and the herds were far away. Rather than let my guest sleep hungry, I slaughtered my beloved black stallion with my own hands to prepare your supper!'

The Roman envoy was struck dumb with awe. He fell at Hatim’s feet and wept: 'By heavens, your fame is but a shadow of your reality! You sacrifice your greatest treasure to feed a stranger without knowing his name.' The emperor, upon receiving the report, acknowledged that Hatim’s open heart was richer than all the gold mines of Rome.
moral: Boundless generosity and selflessness disarm the fiercest envy and elevate a name above all earthly crowns.
